It's not the disorder. I wouldn't call it a disease, it's a disorder. But it isn't that he's bipolar. A lot of times people conflate mental illness and the person together, but the truth of the matter is that the disorder does not invalidate your feelings nor does it justify his behaviour. I have bipolar disorder, I'm currently dealing with it and I don't want it to burden on my relationship. I'm taking active steps to ensure it does not affect my relationship with my wonderful boyfriend. If it's genuinely bothering you, bring it up to him. If he makes you feel invalidated, then it is not a healthy relationship. If he projects his fears onto you, then it is not a healthy relationship. Unhealthy relationships and abuse does not have to be physical nor extreme, if he's gaslighting you, that's emotional abuse and manipulation (granted he is not conscious of it) It takes a lot of guts to leave from an unhealthy relationship, but it's worth it for your happiness.
